question:
Which of the following Articles of the Constitution mentions that, “There shall be paid to the Judges of the Supreme Court, such salaries as may be determined by the Parliament by law, and until provision in that behalf is so made, such salaries as are specified in the Second Schedule”?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: 125
127
124
126
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 125

Explanation:
Article 125 of the Indian Constitution deals with the salaries and allowances of the Judges of the Supreme Court. It states that Judges shall receive salaries as determined by Parliament, and until such provision is made, salaries specified in the Second Schedule shall be paid. This provision ensures the financial independence of the judiciary, a crucial aspect of judicial independence. Under Article 125, the salaries and allowances of Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, ensuring they are not subject to budgetary uncertainties.

Extra Facts:
Article 124 relates to the establishment of the Supreme Court, while Article 126 deals with the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice. Article 127 provides for the appointment of 'ad-hoc Judges' in the Supreme Court. Any changes to the salaries of Judges can only be made by Parliament, and such changes cannot be detrimental to the Judges during their tenure. This safeguard is vital for maintaining judicial independence.

question_hi:
संविधान के निम्नलिखित में से किस अनुच्छेद में उल्लेख किया गया है कि, "उच्चतम न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों को ऐसे वेतनों का संदाय किया जाएगा जो संसद, विधि द्वारा, अवधारित करे और जब तक इस निमित्त इस प्रकार उपबंध नहीं किया जाता है तब तक ऐसे वेतनों का संदाय किया जाएगा जो दूसरी अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट हैं।"?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: 125
127
124
126
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है 125

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 125 उच्चतम न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों के वेतन और भत्तों से संबंधित है। यह अनुच्छेद कहता है कि न्यायाधीशों को संसद द्वारा निर्धारित वेतन मिलेगा, और जब तक संसद द्वारा कोई प्रावधान नहीं किया जाता, तब तक दूसरी अनुसूची में निर्दिष्ट वेतन दिया जाएगा। यह प्रावधान न्यायपालिका की वित्तीय स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करता है, जो न्यायिक स्वतंत्रता का एक महत्वपूर्ण पहलू है। संविधान के अनुच्छेद 125 के तहत, न्यायाधीशों के वेतन और भत्ते भारत की संचित निधि पर भारित होते हैं, जिससे यह सुनिश्चित होता है कि उन्हें किसी बजटीय अनिश्चितता का सामना न करना पड़े।

Extra Facts:
अनुच्छेद 124 उच्चतम न्यायालय के गठन से संबंधित है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 126 कार्यवाहक मुख्य न्यायाधीश की नियुक्ति से संबंधित है। अनुच्छेद 127 उच्चतम न्यायालय में 'अस्थायी न्यायाधीशों' की नियुक्ति की बात करता है। न्यायाधीशों के वेतन में किसी भी प्रकार का संशोधन केवल संसद द्वारा ही किया जा सकता है, और यह संशोधन न्यायाधीशों के कार्यकाल के दौरान उनके लिए प्रतिकूल नहीं हो सकता है। यह प्रावधान न्यायिक स्वतंत्रता को बनाए रखने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।

question:
The Article 371A deals with the special provision with respect to which of the following states?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Assam
Manipur
Nagaland
Sikkim
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nagaland

Explanation:
Article 371A of the Indian Constitution is a special provision applicable exclusively to the state of Nagaland. It was inserted by the 13th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962. This article safeguards the tribal customs, social practices, and land rights of the Naga people. Under this provision, any law passed by the Nagaland Legislative Assembly concerning religious or social practices, land ownership, or administration of tribal areas requires the approval of the Governor (acting on the advice of the Central Government).

Extra Facts:
- Article 371A is specific to Nagaland, while other states like Assam (371B), Manipur (371C), and Sikkim (371F) have their own special provisions.
- Nagaland became the 16th state of India on 1st December 1963.
- This provision was included after negotiations with the Naga People’s Convention (NPC) to protect Naga autonomy.

☛ Nagaland was which number state of India? → 16th
☛ When was Nagaland established as a state? → 1st December 1963
question_hi:
अनुच्छेद 371क निम्नलिखित में से किस राज्य के संबंध में विशेष उपबंध से संबंधित है ?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options_hi: असम
मणिपुर
नागालैंड
सिक्किम
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है नागालैंड

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 371A भारतीय संविधान का एक विशेष उपबंध है जो नागालैंड राज्य के लिए लागू होता है। यह अनुच्छेद 1962 के 13वें संवैधानिक संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। इसके तहत, नागालैंड की जनजातीय परंपराओं, सामाजिक व्यवस्था और कानूनों को संरक्षण प्रदान किया गया है। इसके अंतर्गत, नागालैंड के धार्मिक या सामाजिक प्रथाओं, भूमि और संसाधनों के स्वामित्व तथा नागा जनजातियों के स्वशासन से संबंधित मामलों में राज्य विधानमंडल के कानूनों को लागू करने के लिए केंद्र सरकार की सहमति आवश्यक है।

Extra Facts:
- अनुच्छेद 371A केवल नागालैंड पर लागू होता है, जबकि अन्य राज्यों जैसे असम (371B), मणिपुर (371C), और सिक्किम (371F) के लिए अलग-अलग विशेष उपबंध हैं।
- नागालैंड को 1 दिसंबर 1963 को भारत का 16वां राज्य बनाया गया था।
- नागा पीपल्स कन्वेंशन (NPC) के साथ हुए समझौते के बाद इस अनुच्छेद को संविधान में शामिल किया गया था।

question:
In which of the following articles, "Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment" is mentioned?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Article 14
Article 17
Article 15
Article 16
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 16

Explanation:
Article 16 of the Indian Constitution, part of Part-III (Fundamental Rights), deals with 'Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment'. It guarantees equal opportunity to all citizens in government jobs and prohibits discrimination based on religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, or residence. It also empowers the state to provide reservation for backward classes, SCs, and STs (Article 16(4)). This article is an extension of the Right to Equality (Article 14) and specifically applies to public employment matters.

Extra Facts:
- Article 16(4A) was added by the 77th Amendment (1995), enabling reservation in promotions for SCs and STs.
- The 85th Amendment (2001) introduced the concept of 'consequential seniority' for reserved category employees in promotions.
- Article 335 mandates maintaining administrative efficiency while considering the claims of SCs/STs.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ Which article abolishes untouchability in India? → Article 17
☛ Under which article can the state make special provisions for women and children? → Article 15(3)
☛ Which article ensures 'equality before law'? → Article 14
☛ What does Article 16(4) pertain to? → Reservation for backward classes
question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से किस अनुच्छेद में, "सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र में रोजगार से संबंधित मामलों में अवसर की समानता" का उल्लेख किया गया है?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 14
अनुच्छेद 17
अनुच्छेद 15
अनुच्छेद 16
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 16

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 16 भारतीय संविधान के भाग-III (मौलिक अधिकार) में शामिल है और यह 'लोक नियोजन के विषय में अवसर की समानता' से संबंधित है। यह अनुच्छेद सभी नागरिकों को सरकारी नौकरियों में समान अवसर प्रदान करता है और धर्म, जाति, लिंग, वंश, जन्म स्थान या निवास के आधार पर भेदभाव को प्रतिबंधित करता है। इसके अंतर्गत, राज्य को पिछड़े वर्गों, अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लिए आरक्षण देने का अधिकार भी दिया गया है (अनुच्छेद 16(4))। यह अनुच्छेद समानता के अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14) का विस्तार है और विशेष रूप से सार्वजनिक रोजगार से जुड़े मामलों में लागू होता है।

Extra Facts:
- अनुच्छेद 16(4A) संविधान के 77वें संशोधन (1995) द्वारा जोड़ा गया, जिसने अनुसूचित जातियों और जनजातियों को पदोन्नति में आरक्षण देने का प्रावधान किया।
- 85वें संशोधन (2001) ने पदोन्नति में आरक्षण के मामले में 'कन्डोन ऑफ सीनियरिटी' (वरिष्ठता का लाभ) को बरकरार रखा।
- अनुच्छेद 335 राज्य को अनुसूचित जातियों और जनजातियों के दावों को ध्यान में रखते हुए प्रशासनिक दक्षता बनाए रखने का निर्देश देता है।

question:
Which of the following Rights is mentioned in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty
Right against Exploitation: Prohibition of trafficking in human beings and forced labour
Right to Equality: Equality before law
Right to Freedom of Religion: Freedom to manage religious affairs
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty

Explanation:
Article 21 of the Indian Constitution deals with the 'Protection of Life and Personal Liberty'. It is a fundamental right that ensures no person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law. The Supreme Court has expanded its scope through landmark judgments like Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India (1978), where it ruled that the 'right to life' includes the right to live with dignity, not merely survival.

Extra Facts:
◼ Article 21 is part of Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution.
◼ Under this article, the SC has recognized rights like clean environment, health, education, privacy, and shelter.
◼ Article 21A (86th Amendment, 2002) grants free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14 years.

☛ Article 21A is related to which right? → Right to Education
☛ Maneka Gandhi case is associated with which article? → Article 21

question_hi:

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार : जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता की सुरक्षा

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 21 'जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता के संरक्षण' से संबंधित है। यह एक मौलिक अधिकार है जो यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि किसी व्यक्ति को कानून द्वारा स्थापित प्रक्रिया के बिना उसके जीवन या व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता से वंचित नहीं किया जा सकता। इस अनुच्छेद की व्याख्या सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने कई महत्वपूर्ण निर्णयों में विस्तार से की है, जैसे मेनका गांधी बनाम भारत संघ (1978) के मामले में, जहाँ अदालत ने कहा कि 'जीवन का अधिकार' केवल जीवित रहने का अधिकार नहीं है, बल्कि गरिमापूर्ण जीवन जीने का अधिकार भी है।

Extra Facts:
◼ अनुच्छेद 21 को संविधान के भाग III (मौलिक अधिकार) में शामिल किया गया है।
◼ इस अनुच्छेद के तहत, सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने प्रदूषण मुक्त वातावरण, स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा, गोपनीयता, आवास जैसे अधिकारों को भी मान्यता दी है।
◼ अनुच्छेद 21A (86वाँ संशोधन, 2002) 6-14 वर्ष के बच्चों को मुफ्त और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का अधिकार देता है।

question:
Which article of Indian Constitution is related with the Conduct of business of the Government of a State?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: 132
178
144
166
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 166

Explanation:
Article 166 of the Indian Constitution deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a State. This article specifies the manner in which the Governor of a state shall exercise the executive functions of the state government. It states that all executive actions of the state government shall be taken in the name of the Governor, but the real power lies with the Council of Ministers. Additionally, it outlines the procedure for the Chief Minister to keep the Governor informed about administrative decisions.

Extra Facts:
- While Article 166 pertains to state governments, Article 77 governs the conduct of business of the Central Government.
- The validity of orders issued in the Governor’s name is protected under Article 166(2), which states that if an order is issued as per the procedure prescribed by the Governor, its validity cannot be questioned in court.

☛ To whom is the information about state government business communicated? → The Governor
☛ Who holds the real executive power in a state government? → The Council of Ministers

question:
Under which article of the Constitution, the Supreme Court of India may issue a writ for enforcement of Fundamental Rights?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Article 30
Article 139
Article 44
Article 32
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 32

Explanation:
Article 32 of the Indian Constitution grants citizens the right to directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. It is termed as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' (as per Dr. B.R. Ambedkar). This article empowers the Supreme Court to issue five types of writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto. It is a Fundamental Right itself and cannot be abrogated even by a constitutional amendment (Kesavananda Bharati Case, 1973).

Extra Facts:
• Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs, but it is not restricted to Fundamental Rights alone.
• Article 32 applies only to violations of Fundamental Rights, whereas Article 226 is broader and covers legal rights as well.
• The Supreme Court expanded the scope of Article 32 in the Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India (1978) case.

☛ Which writ releases a person from unlawful detention? → Habeas Corpus
☛ Under which article can Fundamental Rights be suspended? → Article 359

Ambedkar के शब्दों में) कहा जाता है। यह अनुच्छेद सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को पाँच प्रकार की रिटें जारी करने की शक्ति प्रदान करता है: बंदी प्रत्यक्षीकरण (Habeas Corpus), परमादेश (Mandamus), प्रतिषेध (Prohibition), उत्प्रेषण (Certiorari), और अधिकार पृच्छा (Quo Warranto)। यह एक मौलिक अधिकार है और इसे संविधान संशोधन द्वारा भी समाप्त नहीं किया जा सकता (केसवानंद भारती मामला, 1973)।

question:
According to Article _____, there shall be equality of opportunities for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: 18
19
17
16
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 16

Explanation:
Article 16 of the Indian Constitution deals with equality of opportunity in public employment. It ensures that all citizens have equal opportunities in matters of employment or appointment to any office under the State. Discrimination based on religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, residence, or any of these grounds is prohibited under this article. However, the State is also empowered to provide reservations for backward classes, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes (Article 16(4)). This is a fundamental right and is closely linked with Article 14 (Right to Equality) and Article 15 (Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, caste, sex, etc.).

Extra Facts:
◼ Article 16(4A) was added by the 77th Constitutional Amendment (1995), allowing reservations in promotions for SCs and STs.
◼ Article 16(4B) was introduced by the 81st Amendment (2000), permitting the carry-forward of unfilled reserved vacancies.
◼ In the Indra Sawhney Case (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that reservations should not exceed 50% (except in extraordinary cases).

question:
Which Article of the Indian Constitution is related with the Executive powers of the Union?

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: 53

57

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 53

Explanation:
Article 53 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Executive powers of the Union. It states that the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him. Under this Article, the President is also designated as the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces. This Article is part of Part V (The Union) of the Constitution and ensures that executive powers are exercised within the constitutional framework.

Extra Facts:
- Article 74 provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President, headed by the Prime Minister.
- Article 75 deals with the appointment, removal, and duties of Ministers.
- Article 52 defines the position of the President of India, while Article 53 clarifies his executive powers.
- The Constitution does not decentralize executive powers but shares them between the President and the Prime Minister.

question:
Article 17 of the Constitution of India deals with ______.

[SSC GD 2022]
options: abolition of titles
equality before law
abolition of untouchability
right to education
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is abolition of untouchability

Explanation:
Article 17 of the Indian Constitution deals with the 'abolition of untouchability'. This article abolishes untouchability and prohibits its practice in any form. It is part of the Fundamental Rights (Part-III) under the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18). The objective of abolishing untouchability is to ensure social justice and equality. Violation of this provision is punishable by law.

Extra Facts:

- This article is a result of the efforts of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, who emphasized the eradication of untouchability from society.
- Article 35 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to make laws related to untouchability.

question:
Which Article of the Constitution of India states that the Parliament consists of the President of India and the two Houses of Parliament known as Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and House of the People (Lok Sabha)?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options:
Article 62

Article 79

Article 67

Article 73
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 79

Explanation:
Article 79 of the Indian Constitution defines the structure of Parliament. It states that the Parliament consists of the President and two Houses: the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha). This provision is part of Part V (Articles 79 to 122) of the Constitution, which deals with the Union Legislature. The structure ensures a federal balance between the Centre and the States.

Extra Facts:
◉ The three components of Parliament (President, Rajya Sabha, and Lok Sabha) derive their powers from different constitutional articles.
◉ Article 80 deals with the composition of Rajya Sabha and the election of its members, while Article 81 defines the structure of Lok Sabha.
◉ Parliament has powers to make laws, control finances, and oversee the executive.

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 79 संसद की संरचना को परिभाषित करता है। यह अनुच्छेद स्पष्ट करता है कि संसद में राष्ट्रपति और दो सदन होते हैं: राज्य सभा (काउंसिल ऑफ स्टेट्स) और लोकसभा (हाउस ऑफ द पीपल)। यह प्रावधान संविधान के भाग V (अनुच्छेद 79 से 122) में शामिल है, जो संघीय विधायिका से संबंधित है। संसद की इस संरचना का उद्देश्य संघीय प्रणाली को बनाए रखना और केंद्र व राज्यों के बीच संतुलन स्थापित करना है।

question:
_________of the Constitution of India lays down the qualifications for the membership of Parliament.

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Article 84
Article 81
Article 83
Article 82
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 84

Explanation:
Article 84 of the Indian Constitution lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). According to this, a person must fulfill the following conditions to become a member of Parliament:
1. He must be a citizen of India and take an oath prescribed by the Election Commission.
2. The minimum age for Lok Sabha is 25 years and for Rajya Sabha is 30 years.
3. He must fulfill other qualifications as prescribed by Parliament.
Article 81 deals with the composition of Lok Sabha, Article 83 with the duration and sessions of Parliament, and Article 82 with the delimitation of constituencies.

Extra Facts:
- Disqualifications for membership of Parliament are given in Article 102, such as being insolvent, of unsound mind, or holding foreign citizenship.
- The Representation of the People Act, 1951 also elaborates on the qualifications and disqualifications of MPs.
- Article 101 deals with the vacation of seats or resignation of MPs.

question:
Which Article of the Constitution of India grants power to the President to appoint Judges of the Supreme Court?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Article 124(2)
Article 123(1)
Article 127(3)
Article 128(4)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 124(2)

Explanation:
Article 124(2) of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to appoint judges of the Supreme Court. According to this provision, the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and other judges are appointed by the President after consultation with such judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts as the President deems necessary. However, in practice, the advice of the CJI and senior judges plays a crucial role, as established in the Three Judges Cases (1981, 1993, 1998), which led to the evolution of the Collegium System.

Extra Facts:
◼ Article 124(3) specifies the qualifications for a Supreme Court judge, such as being a High Court judge or having 10 years of advocacy experience.
◼ Article 127 deals with the appointment of ad-hoc judges, while Article 128 allows retired judges to sit temporarily.
◼ The Collegium System, recognized in the Second Judges Case (1993), is an informal mechanism where senior judges recommend judicial appointments.

question:
Which article of the Indian Constitution empowers joint sitting of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha under certain circumstances?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Article 100
Article 156
Article 108
Article 75
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 108

Explanation:
Article 108 of the Indian Constitution provides for a joint sitting of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. This is convened when there is a deadlock between the two Houses over an ordinary bill (not a Money Bill or Constitutional Amendment Bill). If the Rajya Sabha rejects or amends a bill passed by the Lok Sabha, the President can summon a joint session presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. Decisions are taken by a simple majority. This mechanism is a unique feature of India’s parliamentary system to resolve disputes.

Extra Facts:
- Joint sittings apply only to ordinary bills, not Money Bills (Article 110) or Constitutional Amendment Bills (Article 368).
- Only three joint sittings have been held so far (1961, 1978, 2002).
- Article 100 deals with voting in Houses, while Article 75 relates to the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.

☛ How many joint sittings have been held so far? → 3

question:
The Indian parliament has power to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse through which article of the Indian constitution?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: 304
300 A
303
302
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 302

Explanation:
Article 302 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to impose restrictions on trade, commerce, and intercourse. This article allows the Union government to impose restrictions on trade and commerce in the public interest. However, this power is subject to Article 301 (which guarantees freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse). Restrictions imposed by Parliament are also subject to judicial review.

Extra Facts:
- Article 301 ensures freedom of trade and commerce throughout India, but this freedom is not absolute.
- Article 303 prohibits discriminatory restrictions between states, while Article 304 allows states to impose reasonable restrictions in public interest.
- Article 300A deals with the right to property, not trade and commerce.

question:
Article 20 of the Constitution of India deals with ……………………

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: protection of life and personal liberty
protection in respect of conviction for offences
abolition of untouchability
right to education
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is protection in respect of conviction for offences

Explanation:
Article 20 of the Indian Constitution deals with protection in respect of conviction for offences. It ensures three fundamental safeguards:
1. Protection against ex-post facto laws – No person can be convicted for an act that was not an offence at the time of its commission.
2. Protection against double jeopardy – No person can be punished twice for the same offence.
3. Protection against self-incrimination – No person can be compelled to be a witness against themselves.

This article provides judicial protection to citizens under fundamental rights and prevents arbitrary legal actions.

Extra Facts:
- Article 20 applies only to criminal cases, not civil or tax matters.
- Article 21 relates to the protection of life and personal liberty, while Article 17 abolishes untouchability, and Article 21A guarantees the right to education.
- The Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) case expanded the interpretation of Article 21, defining it as the 'right to live with dignity'.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 20 अपराधों के लिए दोषसिद्धि के संबंध में संरक्षण प्रदान करता है। यह अनुच्छेद तीन महत्वपूर्ण सिद्धांतों को सुनिश्चित करता है:
1. पश्चात् कानूनों के खिलाफ संरक्षण (Ex-post facto law) – किसी व्यक्ति को उस समय प्रभावी कानून के अनुसार अपराध नहीं होने पर भी बाद में बनाए गए कानून के तहत सजा नहीं दी जा सकती।
2. दोहरे दंड से संरक्षण (Double jeopardy) – एक ही अपराध के लिए किसी व्यक्ति को दो बार दंडित नहीं किया जा सकता।
3. स्व-अभिशंसन के खिलाफ संरक्षण (Self-incrimination) – किसी व्यक्ति को स्वयं के खिलाफ गवाही देने के लिए मजबूर नहीं किया जा सकता।

यह अनुच्छेद मौलिक अधिकारों के तहत नागरिकों को न्यायिक सुरक्षा प्रदान करता है और मनमानी कार्यवाही को रोकता है।

question:
In May 2023, the Supreme Court interpreted which article related to the governance structure of Delhi, which outlines the principles of federalism, participatory democracy and collective responsibility?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Article 226
Article 323A
Article 243B
Article 239AA
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 239AA

Explanation:
In May 2023, the Supreme Court interpreted Article 239AA, which deals with the governance structure of Delhi. This article was inserted into the Constitution through the 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991, granting Delhi the status of a National Capital Territory (NCT). The Court emphasized the principles of federalism, participatory democracy, and collective responsibility under this article. The ruling clarified that the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers of Delhi have authority over administrative matters, but the Central Government retains control over subjects like land, police, and public order. This judgment highlights the importance of federal structure and state autonomy.

Extra Facts:
Article 239AA provides for a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers in Delhi, though it is not a full-fledged state. The article also mandates that the Lieutenant Governor (LG) must act on the advice of the Council of Ministers, except in specific matters. The 2018 Supreme Court verdict reinforced that the LG should not act independently unless exceptional circumstances arise. This article is crucial for understanding Centre-State relations and constitutional balance.

question:
Preventive detention is a part of which article of the Indian Constitution?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: 25
22
28
26
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 22

Explanation:
Preventive Detention is a part of Article 22 of the Indian Constitution. This article deals with the protection against arrest and detention, particularly in cases where a person is detained not for a committed crime but to prevent them from committing a crime in the future. Article 22 provides safeguards such as informing the detainee of the grounds of arrest and the right to legal representation. It is an exception to the fundamental right to life and personal liberty under Article 21. Preventive detention laws are used to maintain public order and national security.

Extra Facts:
1. Under Article 22(4), preventive detention cannot exceed three months unless an advisory board approves an extension.
2. Laws like the National Security Act (NSA), 1980 and the Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA), 2002 are based on preventive detention provisions.
3. The detainee must be informed of the detention grounds as soon as possible, though not necessarily immediately at the time of arrest.

निवारक निरोध (Preventive Detention) भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 22 का भाग है। यह अनुच्छेद व्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता और जीवन के अधिकार से संबंधित है, जिसे अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत संरक्षित किया गया है। अनुच्छेद 22 में गिरफ्तारी और निरोध से संबंधित सुरक्षा उपायों का उल्लेख है, जिसमें निवारक निरोध के मामलों में विशेष प्रावधान शामिल हैं। निवारक निरोध का अर्थ है किसी व्यक्ति को किसी अपराध के आरोप में नहीं, बल्कि भविष्य में अपराध करने की संभावना के आधार पर हिरासत में लेना। यह प्रावधान राज्य को सार्वजनिक व्यवस्था और सुरक्षा के हित में ऐसी कार्रवाई करने की अनुमति देता है।

Extra Facts:
1. अनुच्छेद 22 के तहत, निवारक निरोध के मामले में व्यक्ति को हिरासत के कारणों से अवगत कराना अनिवार्य है, और उसे अपने पक्ष में प्रतिनिधित्व करने का अधिकार है।

question:
Article_______of the Constitution of India deals with provisions related to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: 222(1)
244(1)
222(2)
244(2)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 244(1)

Explanation:
Article 244(1) of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. This article gives effect to the provisions of the Fifth Schedule, which primarily governs the administration of Scheduled Areas in various states of India. Under this, the President has the authority to declare any area as a Scheduled Area and make special administrative arrangements for them. The objective is to protect the interests of tribal communities and ensure their socio-economic development.

Extra Facts:
- Article 244(2) pertains to the Sixth Schedule, which administers tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
- Under the Fifth Schedule, Governors are given special powers, including the authority to make separate laws for Scheduled Areas.
- Article 339 of the Constitution provides for the appointment of a commission by the President to oversee the welfare of Scheduled Tribes.

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 244(1) अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के प्रशासन और नियंत्रण से संबंधित है। यह अनुच्छेद पाँचवीं अनुसूची के प्रावधानों को लागू करता है, जो मुख्य रूप से भारत के विभिन्न राज्यों में अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों के प्रशासन से संबंधित है। इसके तहत, राष्ट्रपति को यह अधिकार है कि वह किसी राज्य में अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों को घोषित कर सकते हैं और उनके लिए विशेष प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था बना सकते हैं। इसका उद्देश्य आदिवासी समुदायों के हितों की रक्षा करना और उनके सामाजिक-आर्थिक विकास को सुनिश्चित करना है।

- संविधान के अनुच्छेद 339 में अनुसूचित जनजातियों के कल्याण के लिए राष्ट्रपति द्वारा आयोग गठित करने का प्रावधान है।

question:
Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all the courts within the territory of India ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Article 151
Article 147
Article 137
Article 141
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 141

Explanation:
Article 141 of the Indian Constitution, under Part V (The Union), states that 'the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India.' This article gives statutory authority to the Supreme Court's judgments and ensures judicial uniformity. It constitutionalizes the doctrine of 'Judicial Precedent,' making it mandatory for lower courts to follow the Supreme Court's rulings.

Extra Facts:
- The purpose of Article 141 is to ensure legal certainty and judicial stability.
- Article 137 empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgments.
- Article 144 mandates all authorities to act in aid of the Supreme Court.
- Article 142 grants the Supreme Court extraordinary powers to pass orders for complete justice.

options_hi: अनुच्छेद 151

अनुच्छेद 137

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 141

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 141 भारतीय संविधान के भाग V (संघ) के अंतर्गत आता है। यह प्रावधान करता है कि 'सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा घोषित विधि (कानून) भारत के राज्यक्षेत्र के भीतर सभी न्यायालयों पर बाध्यकारी होगी।' यह अनुच्छेद सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के निर्णयों को वैधानिक शक्ति प्रदान करता है और न्यायिक एकरूपता सुनिश्चित करता है। यह 'न्यायिक पूर्ववर्ती (Judicial Precedent)' के सिद्धांत को संवैधानिक मान्यता देता है, जिसके तहत निचली अदालतें सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के फैसलों का पालन करने के लिए बाध्य होती हैं।

Extra Facts:
- अनुच्छेद 141 का उद्देश्य कानूनी निश्चितता और न्यायिक स्थिरता सुनिश्चित करना है।

- अनुच्छेद 144 सभी प्राधिकारियों को सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के आदेशों का पालन करने का निर्देश देता है।
- अनुच्छेद 142 सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को न्याय के हित में आवश्यक आदेश पारित करने की असाधारण शक्ति प्रदान करता है।

question:
Which Article authorises the President to appoint the Governor of a State as the administrator of an adjoining Union territory?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Article 238(2)
Article 231(2)
Article 237(2)
Article 239(2)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 239(2)

Explanation:
Article 239(2) of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to appoint the Governor of a State as the Administrator of an adjoining Union Territory (UT). This provision facilitates efficient administrative management of UTs by utilizing existing state resources and ensuring better coordination. It is aimed at optimizing governance in smaller UTs that may not require a separate administrative setup.

Extra Facts:
- Article 239 deals with the administration of Union Territories.
- Article 239A (added by the 14th Constitutional Amendment, 1962) provides for legislatures and Councils of Ministers in certain UTs like Puducherry and Delhi.
- Article 240 grants the President the power to make regulations for some UTs.
